novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that "a procedure's declarative description (the rule it can recite) and the executable pathway that runs in the forward pass" are distinct and weakly coupled, making its novelty route a same-item procedural dissociation plus a causal coupling/repair account rather than a merely new setting. Searches using "LLM recite rule execute different rule," "declarative procedural knowledge LLM dissociation," "verbalized rule behavior causal tracing," and "chain-of-thought faithfulness activation patching" identified Meta-Cognitive Analysis: Evaluating Declarative and Procedural Knowledge in Datasets and Large Language Models (2024), Turpin et al.'s Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think (2023), and Arithmetic Without Algorithms (2024) as the closest work, but these respectively compare knowledge types, demonstrate unfaithful verbal reasoning, or characterize heuristic execution without positing this same-item representational coupling. Moving from those results to the proposed "recited-rule representation" versus "execution circuit" and testing whether binding the former changes the latter is a substantive natural extension built from established dissociation, probing, patching, and steering ideas, rather than a wholly new interpretability paradigm or an already duplicated claim.
